application-outages.summary: Targets one application or workload by label and blocks ingress and/or egress traffic for a bounded outage window without deleting pods.
good_for: application-level downtime where dependent services should lose access temporarily
cutting ingress, egress, or both for a selected app
testing retries, alerts, failover, and dependency timeout behavior while pods stay running
not_for: deleting pods or containers to force restarts
port-specific filtering on a small set of ports

prefer_instead.when: the goal is to delete or disrupt pod objects themselves
the goal is pod network blocking tied to pod networking behavior or OVS flow handling
the goal is filtering only specific ports or protocols instead of a broader app outage

dns-outage.summary: Blocks only DNS traffic from a target pod so the workload keeps running and general connectivity can remain intact while hostname resolution fails.
good_for: service discovery or hostname resolution failures
breaking DNS lookups over UDP and TCP from one workload
name resolution outages without deleting pods
not_for: general network isolation unrelated to DNS
broad ingress and egress outages for the whole application

prefer_instead.when: the goal is overwhelming a service with TCP SYN traffic rather than blocking DNS
the goal is making the application broadly unreachable instead of only breaking name resolution

http-load.summary: Generates sustained HTTP request traffic against a target endpoint or service to measure latency, throughput, saturation, and error behavior under web load.
good_for: fan-out HTTP or web traffic to a service
latency and error observation under sustained request load
load testing at the application HTTP layer
not_for: packet loss, bandwidth shaping, or latency injection at the network layer
generic node or pod disruption without request generation

prefer_instead.when: the goal is network impairment such as loss, delay, or bandwidth control
the goal is connection flood behavior instead of normal HTTP request load

network-chaos.summary: Applies network impairments such as latency, jitter, loss, duplication, corruption, or bandwidth constraints rather than fully blocking traffic on selected ports.
good_for: degrading network quality without complete service shutdown
testing latency, packet loss, corruption, or limited bandwidth
simulating unreliable networks instead of hard traffic denial
not_for: HTTP request generation or SYN attack traffic

prefer_instead.when: the goal is precise ingress or egress blocking on chosen ports
the goal is generating application traffic rather than impairing the network path
the goal is volumetric SYN traffic to stress a listener

node-scenarios.summary: Runs cloud or platform node lifecycle disruptions such as reboot, stop, start, terminate, or kubelet operations against cluster nodes.
good_for: node reboot, stop, start, terminate, or kubelet lifecycle workflows
cloud-backed or general node disruption scenarios
node availability and lifecycle resilience testing
not_for: bare-metal IPMI or BMC power control specifics
node CPU, memory, or I/O stress only

prefer_instead.when: the target environment is bare metal and the action goes through BMC or IPMI
the goal is blocking traffic on ports rather than lifecycle disruption

node-scenarios-bm.summary: Handles bare-metal node disruption through BMC or IPMI-driven power operations and similar hardware-oriented lifecycle actions.
good_for: bare-metal node power management
IPMI or BMC controlled stop, start, reboot, or power-cycle testing
hardware-backed node lifecycle exercises

prefer_instead.when: the environment is cloud-backed or does not require BMC or IPMI control

pod-network-chaos.summary: Blocks pod ingress and/or egress using pod-network-chaos flow-based network disruption, typically for pod-level traffic denial instead of narrow port filters.
good_for: blocking pod traffic broadly at the pod networking layer
ingress or egress denial for selected pods
testing pod-level isolation where full traffic blocking is desired
not_for: single protocol or single-port filtering only
application-wide outages that are better described at the app level

prefer_instead.when: the goal is filtering only certain ports, interfaces, or directions with more precision
the user is describing an application outage for one workload rather than pod networking mechanics

pod-network-filter.summary: Uses targeted pod-level network filtering for selected ports, protocols, or interfaces rather than broader pod traffic blackholing.
good_for: blocking DNS, SQL, or other specific egress flows from a pod
port- or interface-specific network rules
narrow protocol filtering without fully cutting all pod traffic
not_for: application-wide outages across all app traffic

prefer_instead.when: the goal is broader pod ingress or egress denial instead of specific flow filtering
the intent is explicitly about DNS resolution failure because that scenario already captures the DNS-specific use case
the intent is specifically blocking MySQL or PostgreSQL traffic to Aurora

pod-scenarios.summary: Disrupts pod objects themselves, such as deleting or targeting pods by label, excluded label, or pod name in a namespace.
good_for: deleting pods or forcing pod object disruption
testing restart, reschedule, or replica recovery behavior
targeting pods by label, excluded label, or pod name
not_for: keeping pods alive while only blocking their network traffic
killing one container inside a pod without disrupting the whole pod

prefer_instead.when: the goal is disrupting one container process inside a pod
the pods should stay running while the application becomes unreachable
the goal is network isolation while keeping the pod object present

pvc-scenarios.summary: Focuses on PVC capacity pressure or storage exhaustion style experiments on claims rather than throttling IOPS or bandwidth.
good_for: filling or exhausting a persistent volume claim
storage full conditions on a claim
capacity-related failures instead of throughput shaping
not_for: general node disk stress unrelated to a PVC claim

prefer_instead.when: the goal is limiting bandwidth or IOPS instead of making the claim run out of space

storage-throttle.summary: Limits storage bandwidth or IOPS on PVC-backed volumes using cgroup I/O controls rather than filling the claim to capacity.
good_for: throttling read or write throughput
reducing IOPS or bandwidth on storage
slow storage behavior without exhausting volume space
not_for: making a volume run out of free capacity
PVC fill or storage exhaustion tests

prefer_instead.when: the goal is filling a claim or causing storage exhaustion instead of slowing it down

syn-flood.summary: Generates a TCP SYN flood or connection surge against a target service or host to stress listener resiliency under attack-like traffic.
good_for: SYN flood testing
connection surge or TCP flood behavior
stress against a target listener or service

prefer_instead.when: the user is talking about DNS lookups, hostname resolution, or service discovery failures
the goal is sustained web traffic instead of SYN flood traffic
